key_insight: Impermanent introduces a live, continuously updated benchmark that measures how well time-series forecasting models truly generalize across time, avoiding inflated scores from static train-test splits and test-set contamination.
problem_solved: Existing static benchmarks allow inadvertent contamination and optimistic evaluation of foundation-style forecasting models, giving poor evidence of real-world temporal generalization and robustness to distribution drift.
method: Live evaluation protocol: run models on periodically refreshed, strictly held-out future windows rather than fixed train/test splits to simulate real deployment.
Contamination controls: dataset versioning, submission rules, and isolation of test periods to prevent pretraining or model-selection on future data.

Transparent leaderboard & metrics: continuously updated public leaderboard that tracks performance over time and across drifts, emphasizing temporal generalization metrics (e.g., performance decay, robustness to regime change).
impact: Provides practitioners and researchers with a realistic, contamination-resistant way to compare forecasting models and foundation models over time, improving trust in reported gains and guiding model selection for deployment under temporal drift.
visual_elements: Rolling timeline diagram showing train windows, held-out live test windows, and how the benchmark updates over time
Before/after contamination example: two small charts comparing inflated scores from static splits vs. realistic scores from the live benchmark
Live leaderboard mockup tracking model rankings and performance trajectories across multiple time periods
Heatmap or line chart illustrating performance decay or robustness of several models as the forecast horizon and data regimes change
paper_title: Impermanent: A Live Benchmark for Temporal Generalization in Time Series Forecasting
paper_authors: Azul Garza, Renée Rosillo, Rodrigo Mendoza-Smith, David Salinas, Andrew Robert Williams
